newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Liebscher sees 6-8 nations in EMU in '99.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Liebscher sees 6-8 nations in EMU in '99.

text.p: VIENNA, Oct 28 (Reuter) Austria's central bank president klaus Liebscher said on Monday he expected six to eight countries to be among the first wave of nations joining Europe's future single currency in 1999.

"In the interest of the euro's stability the number of members joining in the firt wave is crucial. I see those countries that are already viewed as the most economically stable as being in the first wave -- six, seven, or eight of them," he told reporters.
"I have no problem with such a small group," he added.
Liebscher declined to say which countries would be in the first group but reiterated Austria would certainly be among them.
"I am convinced that we can reach that goal," Liebscher said.
The central bank president said the strict Maastricht criteria for joining the planned currency union must not be watered down to make it easier for some countries to make the mark.
"A watering down of the criteria is absolutely out of the question and so is a postponement," he said. -- Knut Englemann, Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
